items.title: Lawrence Cotton Interview, 1996-12-10
items.q: The Lord had all arrangements from different parts of the country. And stuff like It made a difference.

ctx.x: John Lee Hooker. I mean, you know, the stuff that he plays. And the other man, Muddy Waters, I mean, the stuff that you were playing, I mean, you couldn't dance to their music. I mean, it was like a concert for them, you know. You sit down and look and listen with them. But when we went up there, a lot of people thought that was uncomfortable. When Lloyd went there, we had guys who could play and read. And like I said, Joe Anderson had arrangements, man. And we took those arrangements and put them up there, man.…

items.title: Lawrence Cotton Interview, 1996-12-10
items.q: Joe Anderson came with his band... we were able to get a few arrangements from his band to go with Lloyd's band

ctx.x: Was that like working for a family when you worked for them?

Well, they never were actually in there. Frank did all the business with everybody because everybody come there, a lot of times bands would get stranded at his place. And he'd make them play music for them living there. Yeah. In fact, Joe Anderson came with his band. He was from Carolina. And he came there, he got stranded with his band so we were able to get a few arrangements from his band to go with Lloyd's band, which was really nice, man. Ray Charles used to live down the street at the club on the Fosters.…
